titleStmt.title: Coding of auditory temporal and pitch information by hippocampal individual cells and cell assemblies in the rat
titleStmt.author: Sakurai

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Coding of auditory temporal and pitch information by hippocampal individual cells and cell assemblies in the rat

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Considering those results, this study concludes that dual coding by hippocampal single neurons and cell assemblies is working in memory processing of pitch and temporal information of auditory stimuli.

span.label: hippocampal cell-assembly coding of auditory pitch and duration
span.quote: This study reports how hippocampal individual cells and cell assemblies cooperate for neural coding of pitch and temporal information in memory processes for auditory stimuli.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Multiple neurons were recorded from the rat pyramidal-cell layers of CA1 and CA3 during the performance of the two tasks.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Individual neurons belong to more than one cell assembly, so an assembly can distinguish two tasks that no single member neuron can distinguish - which is how the rat behaves differently while single-cell activity does not differentiate
span.quote: A solution to this contradiction between the single-neuronal activity and the animal’s behavior is the theory of cell-assembly coding

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Coding a task consists in the neurons of the corresponding assembly becoming correlated in activity while that task is being performed
span.quote: If the model outlined in Fig. 9 is correct, activity correlations among the neurons within each of the cell assemblies are expected when the information, i.e., tasks, are being coded by the cell assemblies.

span.label: The pitch and duration information may in fact be coded first in sensory cortex and only reflected in hippocampus.
span.quote: However, the sensory information of inputs (duration and pitch) and/or the tasks with them might be coded and processed ¢rst in sensory areas and then passed onto and re£ected in the hippocampal formation, because some of the sensory neocortical regions have actually been shown to have high degrees of neuronal dynamics underlying cell-assembly coding (e.g., Nicolelis et al., 1998; Ghazanfar and Nicolelis, 1999; Jancke et al., 1999).

span.label: Recording within one region cannot capture assemblies that are distributed across regions.
span.quote: Besides these investigations within regions of interest, investigation of a global cell assembly among plural regions is necessary, because ensemble coding by cell assemblies can be di¡use (Sakurai, 1996b, 1999a; Singer, 1999; Singer et al., 1997).

span.label: Whether the dual-coding scheme generalises beyond hippocampus is untested here.
span.quote: Other brain regions should also be studied, as dual coding with cell assembly might be common across many di¡erent brain regions.

span.label: Neuron pairs with fewer than 2000 combined discharges were excluded from the cross-correlation analysis.
span.quote: Because constructing cross-correlograms requires large enough numbers of neuronal discharges, neuron pairs whose combined total numbers of discharges were less than 2000 during a task were not included in the samples, as in the previous study (Sakurai, 1996a).

span.label: The cell-assembly model is described as supported by the correlation analysis, not established by it.
span.quote: Cross-correlation analysis among activities of simultaneously recorded multiple neurons supported the suggested cell-assembly model

span.label: The interpretation of temporal coding rests on an imported philosophical argument.
span.quote: His philosophical argument suggests that, though there must be real independent time in this world, we have a strong tendency to perceive or recognize time not as independent information but as information concomitant with other physical attributes of stimuli around us

span.label: Bergson's philosophical account of time perception is imported as the interpretive model for why duration is never coded on its own but always alongside another stimulus attribute
span.quote: These non-independent processes for the coding of time in the working brain support Henri Bergson’s theory about the perception of time (Bergson, 1889).

span.label: the division of labour - TWO LEVELS, TWO OBJECTS, IN ONE SENTENCE: single neurons encode the auditory pitches and temporal lengths themselves, while cell assemblies encode the TYPE OF TASK - the context in which that information is processed - so 'the hippocampus codes pitch' is true at one level and beside the point at the other
span.quote: The single neurons encode both auditory pitches and their temporal lengths and the cell assemblies encode types of tasks (contexts or situations) in which the pitch and the temporal information are processed

span.label: dual coding - A BORROWED NAME, ATTRIBUTED: the paper states the phenomenon HAS BEEN CALLED dual coding and cites the source, then reports it demonstrated in several brain regions, so the term arrives with a history rather than being coined here; the citation itself is cut from the span because the staged text mangles the author name
span.quote: This phenomenon has been called ‘dual coding’

span.label: the cell-assembly model's standing - SUPPORTED BY A CORRELATION: the verification is that cross-correlation analysis among simultaneously recorded neurons supported the suggested model, which is a consistency check rather than an independent measurement of an assembly
span.quote: Cross-correlation analysis among activities of simultaneously recorded multiple neurons supported the suggested cell-assembly model

span.label: extends → Sakurai (1996a) cell-assembly coding model of stimulus-discrimination tasks
span.quote: The present results suggest such overlapping of neurons among cell assemblies, and indicate that each type of task is coded not by single neurons but by cell assemblies comprised of the task-related neurons, as was found in a previous study (Sakurai, 1996a).

span.label: builds-on → dual-coding hypothesis (Arieli et al., 1996; Riehle et al., 1997; de Oliveira et al., 1997)
span.quote: The present model is largely consistent with the hypothesis of dual coding proposed in several recent studies (Arieli et al., 1996; Riehle et al., 1997; de Oliveira et al., 1997), which suggested that single neurons encode types of incoming stimuli and cell assemblies encode types of tasks, situations, contexts and/or inner cognitive functions, to process the incoming stimuli.

span.label: builds-on → Henri Bergson's theory of the perception of time (Bergson, 1889)
span.quote: These non-independent processes for the coding of time in the working brain support Henri Bergson’s theory about the perception of time (Bergson, 1889).

span.label: cell assemblies —contrasted-with→ single neurons
span.quote: The single neurons encode both auditory pitches and their temporal lengths and the cell assemblies encode types of tasks (contexts or situations) in which the pitch and the temporal information are processed

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: The neuronal activity recorded during performance of the tasks was collected from trials on which correct performance was obtained, and was analyzed by sequential comparison of preand post-stimulus ¢ring rates (Wilcoxon signed-rank test) and by comparison between the discriminative stimuli (Kruskal^Wallis H and Mann^Whitney U tests) in each task.

span.label: Kruskal-Wallis test
span.quote: The neuronal activity recorded during performance of the tasks was collected from trials on which correct performance was obtained, and was analyzed by sequential comparison of preand post-stimulus ¢ring rates (Wilcoxon signed-rank test) and by comparison between the discriminative stimuli (Kruskal^Wallis H and Mann^Whitney U tests) in each task.

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: The neuronal activity recorded during performance of the tasks was collected from trials on which correct performance was obtained, and was analyzed by sequential comparison of preand post-stimulus ¢ring rates (Wilcoxon signed-rank test) and by comparison between the discriminative stimuli (Kruskal^Wallis H and Mann^Whitney U tests) in each task.

span.label: chi-squared
span.quote: The proportions in Fig. 4 are signi¢cantly di¡erent (X2(2) = 48.1, P 6 .001).

span.label: confidence interval
span.quote: To test whether the revealed correlations, appearing as peaks in the di¡erence cross-correlograms, are statistically signi¢cant, a band of 99.5% con¢dence limits (Abeles, 1982) for the equivalent, independent Poisson processes is shown for each di¡erence cross-correlogram.

span.label: Every hippocampal neuron that discriminated long from short tones in the duration task was also task-related in the pitch task, without exception.
span.quote: However, without exception, neurons which showed task-related di¡erential activity between the long and short tones in the duration-discrimination task were always task-related neurons in the pitchdiscrimination task.

span.label: Neurons related only to the pitch task were the most numerous class, and not a single neuron was related to the duration task alone.
span.quote: The number of neurons related to only the pitch-discrimination task (P) was largest, followed by the many neurons related to both the durationand pitch-discrimination tasks (DP), but there were no neurons related to the duration-discrimination task alone (D).

span.label: The author infers that temporal information cannot be coded independently by dedicated neurons, whereas pitch information can.
span.quote: These results suggest that temporal information (long or short), in contrast to pitch information (high or low), cannot be coded independently by speci¢c neurons.

span.label: The cell assembly encoding the duration task is not separate but sits entirely inside the assembly encoding the pitch task.
span.quote: The cell assembly encoding the duration-discrimination task was completely contained within the cell assembly encoding the pitch-discrimination task.

span.label: Cross-correlation results matched the predictions of the nested cell-assembly model for 37 of the 48 neuron pairs against 11 that did not, a significant excess.
span.quote: The total number of pairs supporting the hypothesis is 37, whereas that of the other pairs is 11.

span.label: The study concludes for dual coding: single neurons carry both the pitch and the duration of the tones, while cell assemblies carry which task (context) the animal is performing.
span.quote: The single neurons encode both auditory pitches and their temporal lengths and the cell assemblies encode types of tasks (contexts or situations) in which the pitch and the temporal information are processed.

span.label: dual coding
span.quote: This phenomenon has been called ‘dual coding’ (Kru« ger and Becker, 1991), and has been experimentally demonstrated in several brain regions

span.label: characteristic features of single-neuron versus cell-assembly coding
span.term: characteristic features of single-neuron versus cell-assembly coding
span.quote: The characteristic features of single-neuron coding are task-related di¡erential activation of individual neurons and those of cell-assembly coding are functional overlapping of individual neurons and correlation dynamics among the neurons in multiple tasks (Sakurai, 1999a,b).

span.label: cross-correlation analysis
span.quote: Cross-correlation analysis (Perkel et al., 1967) is a method to detect activity correlations and show functional synaptic connections among the neurons in behaving animals

span.label: difference correlograms
span.quote: All results reported here refer to such subtracted crosscorrelograms, that is, ‘di¡erence correlograms’ (Ahissar et al., 1992a,b).

span.label: type of information required for correct performance (temporal duration vs. pitch)
span.term: type of information required for correct performance (temporal duration vs. pitch)
span.quote: Both tasks employed an identical apparatus and discriminative stimuli and di¡ered only in the type of information, i.e., temporal information or pitch information, to be coded and processed for correct performance.

span.label: which of the four discriminative tones is presented on a trial
span.term: which of the four discriminative tones is presented on a trial
span.quote: At the start of each trial, in both tasks, one of the discriminative stimuli (H3, H1, L3, L1) was presented in a random manner.

span.label: presence of significant activity correlation between simultaneously recorded neuron pairs
span.term: presence of significant activity correlation between simultaneously recorded neuron pairs
span.quote: Table 1 summarizes the numbers of neuron pairs showing or not showing signi¢cant correlations of activity during the performance of the tasks.

span.label: apparatus and discriminative stimuli (identical across the two tasks, no task cue)
span.term: apparatus and discriminative stimuli (identical across the two tasks, no task cue)
span.quote: The apparatus and presented stimuli were identical in both tasks and there was no cue that told the rats which task they were performing.

span.label: motivational level (food intake capped so it could not differ between tasks)
span.term: motivational level (food intake capped so it could not differ between tasks)
span.quote: Also, because the total amount of food pellets a rat could eat during both tasks was 5 g at most, motivational changes were unlikely to occur among the tasks in a day.

span.label: body weight held at 90% of ad libitum weight
span.term: body weight held at 90% of ad libitum weight
span.quote: All rats were fed enough lab chow 1^3 h after their daily training or recording session to maintain them at 90% of their ad libitum weight.

span.label: 113 — total hippocampal neurons recorded, split 68 in CA1 and 45 in CA3
span.quote: The total number of recorded neurons was 113, among which 68 were from CA1 and 45 were from CA3.

span.label: 48 — neuron pairs that entered the cross-correlation analysis, 28 from CA1 and 20 from CA3
span.quote: Consequently, the total number of neuron pairs analyzed by the cross-correlation analysis was 48 (28 from CA1, 20 from CA3).

span.label: 37 ... 11 — neuron pairs supporting versus contradicting the nested cell-assembly model
span.quote: The total number of pairs supporting the hypothesis is 37, whereas that of the other pairs is 11.

span.label: X2(2) = 48.1, P 6 .001 — chi-squared test showing the three classes of task-related neurons differ in proportion
span.quote: The proportions in Fig. 4 are signi¢cantly di¡erent (X2(2) = 48.1, P 6 .001).

span.label: 12 — number of 5-month-old male albino rats used
span.quote: A total of 12 5-month-old male albino rats (Sankyo Labs, Toyama, Japan) were used.

span.label: 85 dB ... 10 kHz ... 2 kHz — intensity and the high/low frequencies of the four discriminative tones, presented at 3 s or 1 s
span.quote: The common discriminative stimuli were four 85 dB auditory tones, i.e., 3 s of high (10 kHz) tone (H3), 1 s of high tone (H1), 3 s of low (2 kHz) tone (L3) and 1 s of low tone (L1).

span.label: 85% — correct-trial criterion each rat had to reach in a session before moving on in training
span.quote: Each rat was trained in the duration-discrimination task ¢rst to the criterion of 85% correct trials in a session and then trained in the pitch-discrimination task to the criterion.
